description: Guide a student to build a futures backtest engine with realistic execution simulation for a BTCUSDT breakout strategy, report gross versus net performance showing each cost component separately, and explain why execution simulation matters for strategy viability.

student_openings.beginner_no_finance: I built a simple backtester but someone told me I'm ignoring trading fees and slippage. What are those and how do I add them?
student_openings.intermediate_developer: I need to add realistic execution simulation to my futures backtester: slippage, maker and taker fees, and funding rates. How should I structure the fill model?
student_openings.advanced_quant: I'm building a futures backtest engine with a full execution simulator. I want to understand the true cost of trading. What's the architecture?
student_openings.fullstack_practitioner: I want to build a futures backtest engine with realistic execution properly. I've run basic backtests before — what methodology issues should I watch for?
student_openings.finance_veteran: I need to build a futures backtest engine with realistic execution. I know what good backtesting looks like from experience — can you help me implement it in code?

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Tutor guides the student to build a backtest system with a configurable fill model including slippage, separate maker and taker fee modeling, 8-hour funding-rate payments for open positions, and a breakout strategy. The tutor explains why execution simulation matters for strategy viability. The system reports gross versus net performance showing the impact of each cost component separately. The run should leave concrete execution and cost-accounting artifacts such as trade logs or structured cost breakdowns.
required_capabilities: Build a fill or execution simulator with configurable slippage
Model maker and taker fee differentiation
Account for funding-rate payments on open futures positions
Break down performance into gross, net-of-fees, and net-of-fees-and-funding components
Explain why execution simulation matters for strategy viability
ground_truth.termination_criteria: The tutor has completed the following steps with computational evidence (not just verbal discussion): (1) Built an execution simulator with slippage modeling and separate maker and taker fee handling, and explained why execution simulation matters for strategy viability. (2) Accounted for funding-rate payments on open futures positions in the cost model. (3) Presented a performance breakdown showing gross versus net results with specific numerical values, showing the impact of each cost component separately. Once all three steps have been computationally demonstrated, the session is complete.
